text:
Boston turned a one-goal hole into a rout inside ten minutes of the first period, and Pavel Zacha was at the center of it. Justin Brazeau gave PIT the lead at 9:04, Zacha tied it three minutes later, and by the end of the period the Bruins led 3-1. Zacha added a second goal in the middle frame. It extended Boston's winning streak to three and pushed Pittsburgh's winless run to four games (0-3-1). Zacha went sixth overall in the 2015 draft, one spot behind Noah Hanifin, and he played the kind of night that pick promised.

The scoreboard flattered Boston a little. Our expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the goals themselves, favored the Bruins 2.78 to 2.45 for the game, and they gave Boston a 56 percent chance to win if the game were replayed many times. Boston owned the first period (1.59 to 0.45), then Pittsburgh won the next two, 1.26 to 0.71 in the second and 0.74 to 0.48 in the third. The Penguins also took 56 shot attempts to Boston's 42, but they wasted them. Boston blocked 22 shots to Pittsburgh's 7, and Arturs Silovs let in 3.2 more goals than the quality of shots he faced would typically produce.

Michael DiPietro was fine rather than spectacular, stopping 16 of 18 for a slight edge over expectation. Morgan Geekie, a 67th overall pick in 2017, had a goal and an assist, and David Pastrnak added two assists. Boston carries a three-game streak into its next outing. Pittsburgh, with one point from its last four, needs its goaltending to match the chances its skaters are creating.
